title: As a developer, I can hand the product a natural-language goal and it completes a multi-step web task end to end — navigating, filling forms, and clicking through flows
As an AI agent, I can submit a browser task over a hosted HTTP API and receive the result by polling or webhook, without managing any browser myself
As an automation-engineer, I can compose repeatable multi-step workflows with loops, conditionals, and parameters instead of one-shot prompts
As a developer, I can drive the page through DOM-understanding action primitives (act/click/type on described elements) that survive selector and layout changes
As a developer, I can switch to a vision or computer-use action mode that operates on screenshots for canvases and UIs the DOM path can't handle
As a developer, I can preview candidate actions on the current page (observe/plan) before committing the agent to act
As a developer, I can cache resolved actions or generated code so repeat runs replay deterministically at lower cost and latency than re-prompting the LLM
As a developer, I can persist logged-in browser state in reusable profiles so agents skip the login wall on every subsequent run
As an automation-engineer, I can store credentials in a vault and have the agent complete logins including TOTP/2FA challenges without exposing secrets to the model
As a developer, I can connect my existing Playwright, Puppeteer, or CDP automation code to the product's browsers instead of rewriting it
As an automation-engineer, I can rely on a documented captcha stance — automatic solving, human fallback, or explicit non-support — instead of silent task failures
As an automation-engineer, I can enable stealth fingerprinting and residential or geo-targeted proxies so legitimate automations aren't blocked as bots
As an automation-engineer, I can point to the vendor's published acceptable-use and anti-abuse posture governing what its stealth and automation features may be used for
As an automation-engineer, I can run a fleet of concurrent browser sessions with documented concurrency limits and programmatic session management
As a developer, I can get webhook notifications when tasks and sessions finish instead of polling for status
As a developer, I can extract typed, schema-validated data (Zod/Pydantic-style) from pages the agent visits, not just raw text
As a developer, my agent can download files from and upload files to the sites it operates, with the artifacts retrievable afterwards
As an automation-engineer, I can debug a failed agent run from recorded replays — video, screenshots, step-by-step action timelines
As an automation-engineer, I can watch a session live and take human control mid-run when the agent gets stuck
As a developer, I can run the agent against a local browser on my own machine for development, without any cloud account
As a developer, I can bring my own LLM provider — the framework is model-agnostic rather than locked to one vendor's models
As a developer, I can plug the browser layer into agent frameworks (Claude Agent SDK, Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, CrewAI) through documented adapters
As a developer, I can see transparent per-task or per-browser-hour pricing and documented rate/concurrency limits before committing
